title: Friday, 10:05 p.m.
intro: Town Hall, after hours. The great clock ticks above you like a patient animal.

items.label: Archive box: SEPT 1961
items.text: A box marked in green ink. Inside, one sheet: 'EVACUATION REPORT. 913 persons accounted for. Signed E. Pruitt, 9 Sept, 6 p.m.' The pen leaked. Your thumb comes away green.

items.label: Authority memo, folder 7
items.text: 'Close gates upon first surge. Schedule takes precedence.' Stamped 7 September 1961. Somebody has underlined 'precedence' so hard it went through.

items.label: Behind the clock face
items.text: You climb the ladder. Behind the dial is a movement older than the Hall. The minute-hand pin has been filed flat in one place, so it can't pass 4:12 without a click.

items.label: Council minutes, 1961
items.text: Every month for sixty-three years: 'Nothing to report.' Except one page, 11 September 1961, in a different hand: 'Report: 212.' Nothing else.

items.label: Portrait wall: the Pruitts
items.text: Four grim faces and a fifth hook with no frame. Dust shows where it was.

items.label: Rubber stamp: ACCOUNTED FOR
items.text: A heavy, green, wooden stamp. 'ACCOUNTED FOR.' You stamp the back of your hand. It doesn't wash off.

items.label: Dusty trophy: Best Pageant 1974
items.text: The 1974 pageant was apparently outstanding. The lamp-bearer has been cut out of the photograph.

items.label: Window onto the square
items.text: The square is empty. At 4:12 the clock holds for a minute. You are not here for that. Not tonight.
